title: Information Set Emulation: Causal Certificates for AI Derived EHR Features
abstract: arXiv:2609.17777v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI and large language models can recover clinically meaningful features from electronic health records (EHRs), but predictive usefulness does not establish admissibility for causal inference. We introduce information set emulation: an AI typed lift attaches source evidence, clinical and recording times, decision-time availability, representation version, proposed causal roles, and unresolved ambiguity to extracted features under a locked target trial. Causal certificates record auditable evidence for those roles. Features with unresolved downstream roles are routed to compatible reporting or separate analyses.   Typed evidence defines an observational fiber of causal worlds consistent with the observed law. The locked scalar estimand maps this fiber to a compatible image whose squared Chebyshev radius equals the residual minimax mean squared error when the image is nonempty and compact. translated_title: 信息集仿真：AI衍生电子健康档案特征的因果证书
translated_abstract: 人工智能和大语言模型能够从电子健康档案（EHR）中恢复具有临床意义的特征，但预测上的有用性并不能确立其在因果推断中的可采性。我们提出了信息集仿真方法：一种AI类型化提升机制，在锁定的目标试验下，为提取的特征附加来源证据、临床时间与记录时间、决策时可用性、表征版本、拟议的因果角色以及未解决的歧义。因果证书为这些角色记录可审计的证据。对于下游角色未解决的特征，则被引导至兼容的报告方式或单独的分析。
tldr: 该论文提出“信息集仿真”方法，通过类型化证据与因果证书为AI从电子健康档案中提取的特征提供可审计的因果推断可采性框架，弥合了AI预测能力与因果推断有效性之间的鸿沟。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces "information set emulation," a framework using causal certificates to provide auditable admissibility evidence for AI-derived EHR features, bridging the gap between AI predictive usefulness and valid causal inference.
